engines.name: 2.0L turbo plug-in hybrid (AMG GLC63 S E Performance)

issues.t: Engine failure from a cracked piston on the 2.0L turbo
issues.sym: Sudden loss of power, misfire and check engine lights, heavy white or blue smoke from the exhaust, or a knocking engine, often between 60,000 and 75,000 miles.
issues.why: Owners of 2.0L turbo GLC300s and related Mercedes models have reported pistons cracking and engines failing. No root cause or recall has been announced, and the engine draws the most complaints for this SUV.
issues.next: If the engine suddenly misfires or smokes, stop and have it towed rather than driving on. Keep oil change and service records, which matter if you ask Mercedes for goodwill help.

issues.t: Rear seat belt latch plates slip behind the trim (recall)
issues.sym: A rear outer seat belt buckle tongue disappears behind the side trim, so passengers can't buckle up.
issues.why: The rear outboard latch plates can slide back into the interior paneling.
issues.next: Have a dealer install the free buffer on the trim. Don't seat anyone where the belt can't be used.

issues.t: Driver airbag can go off unexpectedly (recall)
issues.sym: An airbag warning light; in rare cases the driver airbag deploys without a crash.
issues.why: If the steering column clockspring is broken, a static discharge through poorly grounded steering parts can set off the airbag.
issues.next: Have the recall done at a dealer, and get an airbag warning light checked promptly.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator may rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before a crash.
issues.why: The driver airbag inflator housing on some 2018 models may have been made from defective steel and could burst when the airbag deploys.
issues.next: Check your VIN and get the airbag replaced for free right away.

issues.t: Starter current limiter can overheat after repeated start attempts (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke after cranking the engine over and over without it starting.
issues.why: If the engine can't turn over, repeated starting attempts can overheat the starting current limiter, which could melt and cause a fire.
issues.next: Don't keep cranking an engine that won't start. Have the free recall repair done.

issues.t: Stability control unit may be damaged (recall)
issues.sym: Stability control may brake a wheel when it shouldn't, warning lights come on, or the electronic parking brake may not work.
issues.why: The stability control (ESP) unit on some early 2016 SUVs may have been damaged before it was installed.
issues.next: Have the recall checked with your VIN.

issues.t: Steering column switch wiring can chafe (recall)
issues.sym: Possible airbag warning light, unexpected airbag deployment, or the engine stalling.
issues.why: The wiring for the steering column switch may be routed so it rubs and wears through.
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN and reroute or repair the wiring.

issues.t: Headlights aimed too low (recall)
issues.sym: Low beams don't light the road far enough ahead at night.
issues.why: Some headlights were adjusted wrong at the factory.
issues.next: A dealer will re-aim the headlights for free.

issues.t: Panoramic sunroof trim panels can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Wind noise, rattles from the roof, or loose trim around the sunroof edge.
issues.why: Plastic panels at the front and sides of the panoramic sunroof may not be bonded well enough and could separate while driving.
issues.next: Have a dealer inspect and re-bond the panels for free.

issues.t: Front seat belt pretensioners may not work (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom you can see.
issues.why: The front seat belt pretensioners on some 2017 models may not fire in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the belts repaired for free.

issues.t: Front roof panel may not be bonded after a repair (recall)
issues.sym: Wind noise or a loose panel at the front of the roof on panoramic-roof SUVs.
issues.why: On SUVs that had the front roof panel repaired, the panel may not have been bonded correctly and could come off.
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN, especially if the roof or sunroof was repaired before.

issues.t: Emergency call (eCall) system may fail or send the wrong location (recall)
issues.sym: An SOS system warning, or no sign until the system is needed.
issues.why: Software and SIM card faults in the communication module can stop the automatic crash call from working or make it report the wrong location.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check your VIN for open eCall updates; they are free.

issues.t: Front seat belts may be read as unbuckled (recall)
issues.sym: A seat belt warning even when buckled, and the pre-crash safety system may switch off.
issues.why: The system can wrongly detect a fastened front belt as unfastened, disabling PRE-SAFE and the belt pretensioner.
issues.next: Have the free software repair done.

issues.t: Power steering assist can cut out (recall)
issues.sym: Steering suddenly gets much heavier, with a steering warning on the dash.
issues.why: A sensor inside the electric power steering unit, or the wiring between its motor and control unit, can fail.
issues.next: Grip the wheel firmly and slow down. Check your VIN for recalls 18V-840, 19V-822 and 20V-651.

issues.t: Driver airbag module may not be bolted down (recall)
issues.sym: No warning; possibly a rattle from the steering wheel.
issues.why: The driver's front airbag module on some SUVs may not be fastened properly.
issues.next: Have a dealer check and secure it for free.

issues.t: Fuel injectors can leak at the fuel rail (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell from the engine bay.
issues.why: Particles trapped between the fuel rail and injectors during assembly can stop them sealing.
issues.next: Don't drive if you smell fuel strongly. Have the recall done.

issues.t: Turbocharger oil line screws may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Oil leaking near the turbo, smoke from the engine bay or a burning-oil smell.
issues.why: The screws on the turbo's oil feed and return lines may not have been tightened enough.
issues.next: Stop driving if you see smoke and have the recall done.

issues.t: Plug-in hybrid high-voltage wiring can fail and stall the SUV (recall)
issues.sym: The SUV loses drive power or stalls, with hybrid system warnings.
issues.why: The shield on a high-voltage wiring harness may fail under electrical load.
issues.next: Have the recall done promptly. If it stalls, steer to safety.

issues.t: Side crash sensor connectors can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: An airbag warning light may come on.
issues.why: Plugs for the side impact sensors may loosen, which could delay side airbags and belt tensioners in a crash.
issues.next: Have a dealer inspect and secure the connectors for free.

issues.t: Rearview camera image may not appear (recall)
issues.sym: The screen stays black or reboots when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: Software faults in the infotainment system can stop the backup camera image from showing.
issues.next: Use mirrors and look behind you. A free software update fixes it.

issues.t: Headlight connector can let water in (recall)
issues.sym: A headlight that stops working.
issues.why: An electrical connection on the headlights may not be watertight.
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN and fix the connector.

issues.t: Headlights aimed too high and glare other drivers (recall)
issues.sym: Oncoming drivers flash their lights at you.
issues.why: Headlights on some SUVs may be adjusted too high.
issues.next: A dealer will re-aim them for free.

issues.t: Fuel pump can shut down and cut power (recall)
issues.sym: The engine loses power or stalls while driving.
issues.why: The fuel pump may shut down unexpectedly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 23V-445 and 23V-880 and get the free fix.

issues.t: Starter cable can chafe and short on the AMG GLC63 (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or starting problems.
issues.why: The starter power cable can rub against the starter housing and short out.
issues.next: Have the free recall repair done.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump may leak fuel and oil (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel or oil smell or drips under the engine.
issues.why: The wrong screws may have been used on the high-pressure fuel pump, so it can leak near hot engine parts.
issues.next: Stop driving if you smell fuel and have the recall done right away.

issues.t: Windows may not be secured and can detach (recall)
issues.sym: A loose window or windshield, or wind noise around the glass.
issues.why: Front, rear and fixed side windows may not have been bonded properly. The windshield may not support the airbag in a crash.
issues.next: Have the recall checked with your VIN before driving at speed.

issues.t: 80-amp fuses may fail (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of electrical functions or warning lights.
issues.why: Some 80-amp fuses were made incorrectly and can fail. Some cars repaired for this got the wrong fuse box.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 24V-115 and 25V-255.

issues.t: Engine carrier welds can fail (recall)
issues.sym: Clunks from the front, or the SUV feeling unstable.
issues.why: The integral carrier that supports the engine may have poor welds and could fail, affecting control.
issues.next: Have the recall done promptly.

issues.t: Rear differential bolts can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or vibration from the rear, or loss of drive.
issues.why: Bolts holding the rear differential to its carrier may loosen, and the driveshaft could separate.
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN and torque the bolts.

issues.t: Rear roof pillar trim may not protect heads in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom you can see.
issues.why: On SUVs with the panoramic roof, the rear pillar trim may not absorb enough energy if a rear passenger's head hits it.
issues.next: Have a dealer modify the trim and headliner for free.

issues.t: Steering coupling bolt may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or play in the steering, or steering that doesn't respond normally.
issues.why: A bolt on the steering coupling may not have been tightened properly, letting it loosen from the steering rack.
issues.next: Stop driving if steering feels loose and have the recall done.

issues.t: Infotainment restart can blank the instrument display (recall)
issues.sym: The instrument cluster goes dark for a moment while driving, losing the speedometer and warnings.
issues.why: The infotainment control unit can reset while moving, which blanks the driver display.
issues.next: Have the free software update done.

issues.t: Door switch corrosion can let the SUV roll away (recall)
issues.sym: The SUV doesn't recognize the driver's door is open, and the parking brake may not set automatically.
issues.why: A micro-switch in the driver's door lock can corrode and fail to detect an open door.
issues.next: Always put the SUV in Park and set the parking brake yourself until the recall is done.

issues.t: Hybrid starter-alternator software can cut drive power (recall)
issues.sym: Loss of drive power with hybrid warnings.
issues.why: A software error can make the high-voltage starter-alternator control unit fail on the AMG GLC63 S E Performance.
issues.next: Have the free software update done.
issues.eng: 2.0L turbo plug-in hybrid (AMG GLC63 S E Performance)

issues.t: Rattle or grinding on cold start from the camshaft adjusters
issues.sym: A loud rattle or grinding noise for a second or two right after a cold start. Over time it can last longer, and the check engine light may come on, sometimes with slow cranking.
issues.why: The camshaft adjusters (the gears that change valve timing) may not lock in place when the engine first starts. The timing chain and its tensioner can also be worn. Shops see this most often between about 37,000 and 75,000 miles on the 2.0L turbo.
issues.next: Have it checked soon instead of waiting for it to get louder. Ask the shop to inspect the timing chain and tensioner at the same time. Use the oil Mercedes specifies and change it on schedule.

issues.t: Oil leaking from the camshaft solenoids into the wiring
issues.sym: Oil around the top front of the engine, oily electrical plugs on the camshaft solenoids, and sometimes a check engine light or rough idle.
issues.why: The seals inside the camshaft solenoids (electric valves that control valve timing) harden with heat and age. Oil can then seep out and travel along the wiring harness toward the engine computer.
issues.next: Get it fixed before oil reaches the engine computer, which is a far bigger repair. Ask the shop to check the connectors and harness for oil and to match the part to your VIN.

issues.t: Thermostat sticks open or leaks coolant
issues.sym: The engine takes a long time to warm up, the heater is weak, the temperature gauge moves around, a low coolant warning appears, or dried coolant crust shows around the thermostat housing or hoses.
issues.why: The electronic thermostat can fail in the open position, and plastic coolant fittings and hoses can crack after years of heating and cooling. This usually shows up between about 50,000 and 87,000 miles.
issues.next: Only open the coolant cap when the engine is cold, and top up with the coolant Mercedes specifies. If the temperature gauge climbs toward hot, pull over and shut the engine off. Have the leak traced before it gets worse.

issues.t: Cracked piston or cylinder head failure on the 2020-2022 GLC300
issues.sym: A check engine light, sometimes with sputtering, shaking or a rough-running engine. Some owners noticed nothing else before the dealer found the damage, often between about 40,000 and 60,000 miles.
issues.why: Owners of 2020-2022 GLC300s, which use the updated version of the 2.0L turbo, report cracked pistons and cylinder heads that needed replacing. There is no recall. One owner was told Mercedes had a warranty extension for some engines, but their VIN was not included.
issues.next: If the engine shakes or the check engine light flashes, stop driving and have it towed. Ask the dealer whether any warranty extension covers your VIN, and ask Mercedes for goodwill help, with your service records in hand. Owners report dealer quotes of about $10,000 to $16,000.

issues.t: Will not start, with a burst of warning messages
issues.sym: The SUV will not start, often after sitting, and opening the door brings up many warning messages at once. A few owners say the engine shut off while driving.
issues.why: NHTSA reviewed a 2023 GLC300 owner complaint and traced the fault to software in the central powertrain controller, not the 48-volt mild-hybrid battery. Dealers have fixed many cars with software updates, though some owners needed several visits.
issues.next: If it shuts off while driving, steer to a safe spot and call roadside assistance. Ask the dealer to install all available software updates and keep every repair order, which matters if the problem keeps coming back.
